.\wiki\War_System.md:3:War 'N Taxes turns peaceful colony-building into high-stakes geopolitics. Players can declare war on each other's colonies, fight in real-time PvP battles with limited lives, and claim the spoils of victory â€” or suffer devastating economic consequences if they lose.
.\wiki\War_System.md:5:This page covers the full war lifecycle from declaration to aftermath.
.\wiki\War_System.md:7:> **Tip:** To contest a player's *secondary* colony for tax income without triggering a full server-wide war, use the **[Besiege System](Besiege_System)** instead. Besieging is a lighter single-player raid that grants tax vassalage. Primary colonies still require full war.
.\wiki\War_System.md:13:**Command:** `/wnt wagewar <colony>` (optionally `/wnt wagewar <colony> <extortion%>`)
.\wiki\War_System.md:15:Before a colony can declare war, it must meet several prerequisites:
.\wiki\War_System.md:19:- **Target Minimum Guards:** The target colony must also have at least `MinGuardsToWageWar` guards. You cannot declare war on a completely undefended colony.
.\wiki\War_System.md:21:- **Grace Period:** After declaring a war, the attacker is locked out from declaring another for `AttackerGracePeriodMinutes` (default: 120 = 2 hours).
.\wiki\War_System.md:22:- **Concurrent War Lock:** A colony that is already participating in an active war â€” as either attacker or defender â€” cannot start or be pulled into a second war until the current one ends. This prevents a colony from being engaged in two wars simultaneously.
.\wiki\War_System.md:23:- **Primary Colony as Attacker:** When you declare war, the mod selects which of your colonies is put at stake as the attacker. It always prefers your primary (first) colony when it meets the requirements, so your secondary outpost colonies are not wagered unintentionally.
.\wiki\War_System.md:27:- If `WarAcceptanceRequired` is **true** (default): The defender receives a clickable accept/decline prompt. They have 30 seconds to respond. If they decline or the timer expires, the war is cancelled.
.\wiki\War_System.md:28:- If `WarAcceptanceRequired` is **false**: The war begins immediately with no option to refuse.
.\wiki\War_System.md:32:> **Screenshot placeholder:** *Flow diagram showing the war lifecycle: declaration â†’ acceptance prompt â†’ join phase â†’ active combat â†’ victory condition check â†’ outcome (occupation / transfer / vassalization)*
.\wiki\War_System.md:38:The High Stakes system introduces two mechanics that make war risky for **both** sides: Outpost Vulnerability and the Colony Wager.
.\wiki\War_System.md:44:Every player's **first colony** is automatically designated as their **Primary Colony** (capital). Any additional colonies they create are **Secondary Colonies** (outposts). The mod tracks this via `FirstColonyTracker`, persisted in `config/warntax/firstColonyData.json`.
.\wiki\War_System.md:50:1. The war starts immediately â€” no acceptance prompt, no join phase
.\wiki\War_System.md:53:4. If the war timer expires without a clear winner, the defender wins by default
.\wiki\War_System.md:61:When the Colony Wager is enabled, the attacker's colony is put at stake in every war:
.\wiki\War_System.md:68:> **Strategic implication:** You cannot safely bully weaker players. If you attack and lose, your own colony becomes occupied. Think carefully before declaring war.
.\wiki\War_System.md:72:If your colony has been occupied (either from losing a war or from the wager system), you have special privileges to fight back:
.\wiki\War_System.md:74:- You can declare war using your **occupied colony** as the attacker â€” even if that colony no longer meets the normal building/guard requirements
.\wiki\War_System.md:75:- **Building requirements and treasury costs are waived** for reclamation wars
.\wiki\War_System.md:77:- Winning a reclamation war **ends the occupation immediately** and restores full ownership
.\wiki\War_System.md:90:- **Declaration Cost:** Your treasury must hold at least `TreasuryMinPercentOfTarget` (default: 25%) of the target colony's tax balance to declare war. A secondary check requires `TreasuryMinPercentOfOwnTax` (default: 10%) of your own balance, preventing wealthy colonies from cheaply bullying poor ones.
.\wiki\War_System.md:91:- **Active Drain:** During combat, both attacker and defender treasuries drain every minute. The drain mode is set by `TreasuryDrainUsePercent` (default: true). When using percent mode, the drain is `TreasuryDrainPercent` (default: 0.4% of max capacity per minute). When using flat mode, the drain is `TreasuryDrainPerMinute` (default: 10 per minute). At default settings with a full 25,000 treasury, a war can be sustained for approximately 4 hours.
.\wiki\War_System.md:93:- **Auto-Surrender:** If `TreasuryAutoSurrenderEnabled` is true, the war ends in surrender when either side's treasury is fully depleted.
.\wiki\War_System.md:111:Before a war starts, the attacker can demand a one-time payment from the defender to cancel the war:
.\wiki\War_System.md:113:- **Command:** `/wnt wagewar <colony> <percent>` â€” declares war with an extortion demand attached
.\wiki\War_System.md:116:- **Paying:** The defender uses `/wnt payextortion <colonyId>` to pay. This cancels the war and grants the defender temporary immunity (`ExtortionImmunityHours`, default: 4 hours)
.\wiki\War_System.md:117:- **Refusing:** If the defender does not pay in time, the war proceeds normally
.\wiki\War_System.md:123:Once the join phase ends, the war enters active combat. Both sides fight with limited lives and a ticking clock.
.\wiki\War_System.md:128:- **Spectator Mode:** Eliminated players receive a glowing outline visible to all and are switched to spectator. You remain in the war zone until it concludes but have no further influence on the outcome.
.\wiki\War_System.md:134:If `EnablePvPKillEconomy` is true, killing an enemy player during war transfers `PvPKillRewardPercentage` (default: 25%) of the victim's personal balance directly into the killer's account.
.\wiki\War_System.md:138:A persistent boss bar displays the current war state for all participants: attacker lives, defender lives, and remaining time.
.\wiki\War_System.md:142:The war ends when:
.\wiki\War_System.md:151:What happens when the war ends depends on configuration. The outcomes are checked in priority order:
.\wiki\War_System.md:161:- The original owner keeps full control and has `OccupationDurationDays` (default: 7) real-time days to wage a reclamation war
.\wiki\War_System.md:163:- If the Colony Wager is active and the **defender** won, the **attacker's** colony is occupied instead
.\wiki\War_System.md:185:If all territory systems are disabled, the war resolves purely through economic penalties (see section 7).
.\wiki\War_System.md:195:Losing a war has severe economic consequences:
.\wiki\War_System.md:198:- **Stalemate Loss:** If the war ends in a draw, **all** participants lose `WarStalematePercentage` (default: 10%).
.\wiki\War_System.md:199:- **War Exhaustion:** After any war, the colony's tax generation is reduced by `WarTaxReductionPercent` (default: 30%) for `WarTaxFreezeCycles` (default: 3 tax cycles) and then recovers fully over `PostWarRecoveryHours` (default: 48 hours).
.\wiki\War_System.md:200:- **War Immunity:** After losing a war, the defeated colony enters a temporary immunity window. During this period, the colony cannot declare war and cannot be declared upon. This prevents repeated attacks on weakened colonies and gives them time to recover.
.\wiki\War_System.md:201:- **War Reparations:** If a colony loses `ReparationsTriggerLossesCount` (default: 3) wars within a 7-day window, a War Reparations debuff is applied. This slashes tax generation by `ReparationsTaxPenaltyPercent` (default: 20%) for `ReparationsDurationHours` (default: 72 hours). After reparations trigger, the colony enters an additional immunity cooldown to prevent an infinite penalty loop.
.\wiki\War_System.md:207:**Wars survive server restarts and crashes.** All war state â€” player lives, timers, boss bars, and permissions â€” is automatically saved to `config/warntax/active_wars.json` on server shutdown and restored on the next startup.
.\wiki\War_System.md:209:- Remaining war duration is recalculated so the timer resumes where it left off
.\wiki\War_System.md:212:- If a war's timer fully expired during downtime, it is not restored (the war ends naturally)
.\wiki\War_System.md:213:- You **cannot** escape a losing war by restarting the server
.\wiki\War_System.md:214:- When you log in, both the colony **owner and all officers** receive a chat message and on-screen title alert for any active war involving their colonies. This happens whether the war started while you were online or offline.
.\wiki\War_System.md:220:While a war is ongoing, opening the colony management GUI and selecting the affected colony shows a live status entry at the top of the **Events** tab:
.\wiki\War_System.md:223:- Attacker side: **Attacking [Colony Name]** â€” red bar, note that the treasury is actively draining
.\wiki\War_System.md:225:This entry cannot be dismissed. It disappears automatically when the war ends.
.\wiki\War_System.md:231:Either side can propose peace at any time during an active war. There are three proposal types:
.\wiki\War_System.md:235:| `/wnt peace whitepeace` | Propose ending the war with no reparations â€” the status quo is restored |
.\wiki\War_System.md:237:| `/wnt peace surrender` | Unconditionally surrender â€” the war ends with you as the loser, applying all defeat penalties |
.\wiki\War_System.md:243:Wars can involve teams. If players use FTB Teams or similar team systems, allies can participate in wars alongside the primary combatants.
.\wiki\War_System.md:245:- When war is declared, a **Join Phase** allows team members and allies to accept or decline participation
.\wiki\War_System.md:246:- Accepted allies contribute lives to their side and share in victory rewards or defeat penalties
.\wiki\War_System.md:247:- Declined allies are excluded from the war entirely
.\wiki\War_System.md:256:| `/wnt wagewar <colony>` | Declare war on a colony |
.\wiki\War_System.md:257:| `/wnt wagewar <colony> <extortion%>` | Declare war with an extortion demand |
.\wiki\War_System.md:258:| `/wnt war accept <colonyId>` | Accept a war declaration |
.\wiki\War_System.md:259:| `/wnt war decline <colonyId>` | Decline a war declaration |
.\wiki\War_System.md:260:| `/wnt joinwar` | Join an active war on your side |
.\wiki\War_System.md:261:| `/wnt leavewar` | Leave an active war |
.\wiki\War_System.md:262:| `/wnt warinfo` | View details about your current war |
.\wiki\War_System.md:263:| `/wnt payextortion <colonyId>` | Pay the extortion demand to cancel the war |
.\wiki\War_System.md:271:| `/wnt warhistory [colony]` | View war history |
.\wiki\War_System.md:272:| `/wnt warstats` | View your personal war statistics |
.\wiki\War_System.md:278:The defeat penalties in section 7 â€” tax freeze cycles, post-war recovery, reparations, and weariness immunity â€” are covered in full detail on the [War Exhaustion](War_Exhaustion) page, including how the penalties interact when multiple systems are active at once and the config keys that control each threshold.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:8:At the heart of the mod is a dynamic taxation system that rewards active, well-developed colonies.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:10:- **Debt Limits:** A colony can go into debt. When a colony is in debt, raiding it might not be as profitable, or certain negative events could trigger. If the debt reaches a specified limit, the colony will stop generating revenue altogether.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:17:Colonies can declare war on one another, changing interactions from peaceful to hostile. See [War & PvP](War_System) for the full guide.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:18:- **Declaring War:** A colony must satisfy minimum defense requirements (building levels or guard counts) before declaring war, protecting newer colonies from being trivially attacked.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:19:- **High Stakes Rules:** Your first colony (Capital) can only be attacked while you are online. Additional colonies (Outposts) can be attacked even while you are offline â€” guards defend automatically. When `EnableColonyWager` is on, your own colony is also at stake â€” lose the war and your colony becomes occupied by the defender.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:20:- **Extortion:** Before a war starts, the attacker can demand a percentage of the defender's wealth as a one-time payment to cancel the declaration. Paying grants temporary immunity.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:21:- **Occupation:** Winning a war does not instantly transfer the losing colony. Instead the defeated colony enters an **Occupation phase** where the winner collects a share of taxes while the original owner has a set number of real-time days to fight back via a reclamation war. Ownership only transfers if no reclamation war is won within that window. See [Colony Occupation](Occupation_System) for details.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:22:- **Reclamation Wars:** Players whose colonies are occupied can declare war with waived building requirements and treasury costs â€” ensuring they are never permanently locked out of fighting back.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:24:- **Peace Treaties:** Players can propose white peace or demand reparations at any point during a war.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:25:- **War Persistence:** Active wars survive server restarts and crashes. All war state is saved to `config/warntax/active_wars.json` automatically.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:31:- **Requirement to Raid:** Similar to War, raids require specific guard or building thresholds. Protective rules are also placed so veteran towns cannot hopelessly raid infant towns.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:32:- **Tax Stealing:** During a raid, every time you kill a Guard or Militia member, a percentage of the defending colony's accumulated Tax Treasury is stolen directly into the raider's pockets (default: 10% per kill, capped at 50% total).
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:33:- **Citizen Militia:** Unlike vanilla Minecolonies where citizens cower in their homes during attacks, War 'N Taxes arms them! A configurable percentage of citizens convert into temporary Militia who fight alongside Guards. Militia are equipped with wooden swords and use custom combat AI. They revert to civilians when the raid ends.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:34:- **Guard Resistance:** During active raids, guards and militia receive a Damage Resistance buff that reduces incoming damage. The resistance level is configurable and applies for the full duration of the raid. Buildings like Guard Towers, Barracks, Combat Academies, and Archery ranges contribute to the resistance calculation.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:35:- **Defensive Tactics:** Raiding isn't free. Upon death during a raid, an attacker loses a heavy portion of their personal balance as a penalty. Successful defenders receive a bonus (+25% of the attacker's penalty).
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:44:- **Four mission types:** Scout (gather intel), Sabotage (cut target's tax income), Bribe (weaken target guards for their next raid), and Steal (boost your own tax income).
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:46:- If JourneyMap is installed, active missions appear as map waypoints.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:58:To prevent server clutter from inactive players, colonies can be set to "Auto-Abandon" after a configured number of days without Owner/Officer activity.
.\wiki\Features_&_Mechanics.md:60:- Claiming is not free! Initiating a claim triggers a massive *Claiming Raid* where all remaining citizens become hostile militia to defend their home. If the claimer survives the raid, the colony is theirs.

.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:9:Prior to this feature, **all active wars were lost on server stop or crash**. The `ACTIVE_WARS` map lived entirely in memory, meaning any server restart during an ongoing war would silently erase the conflict â€” no winner, no loser, no consequences. Players could also exploit this by forcing a restart to escape a losing war.
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:11:The War Persistence system serializes all active war state to disk on server shutdown and restores it on the next startup, ensuring wars survive restarts and crashes gracefully.
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:21:**Why:** The original constructor calls `initializeGuards()` which scans the colony for guards and generates a fresh `warID`. When restoring a saved war, we need to inject the *exact* values from the save file â€” the original war ID, the original guard counts, the original lives â€” without recalculating anything.
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:24:- The new constructor accepts **all** war state fields (27 parameters) and assigns them directly
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:45:`WarSaveData` is simply a wrapper with a `List<WarSaveEntry>` field called `wars`.
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:52:1. Creates the directory `config/warntax/` if it doesn't exist
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:59:4. Writes the entire `WarSaveData` to `config/warntax/active_wars.json` using Gson with pretty-printing
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:60:5. Logs the count of wars saved
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:62:**If no wars are active**, an empty list is written (which loads cleanly as a no-op).
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:69:1. Checks if `config/warntax/active_wars.json` exists â€” if not, returns silently
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:78:This is the most complex method. It rebuilds a single war from its save entry.
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:83:- If the defender colony no longer exists, the war is **skipped** (logged as warning)
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:84:- If the attacker colony was saved but no longer exists, the war is also **skipped**
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:88:- Invalid status strings cause the war to be skipped
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:97:- **INWAR status:** Calculates `warStartTime + warDurationMs`. If the current time exceeds this, the war expired during downtime and is **skipped** (not restored).
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:98:- **JOINING status:** If the join phase end time has passed, the war is **promoted to INWAR** immediately with `warStartTime` set to now. The join phase is not re-run.
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:109:**Step 7 â€” State Restoration (INWAR wars):**
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:110:- Reapplies war glow effects to all participants
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:113:- Calls `startWarCountdown()` to resume the war timer
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:117:**Step 7b â€” State Restoration (JOINING wars):**
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:120:- Schedules a `TickScheduler.scheduleDelayed()` callback for when the join phase expires, which transitions the war to INWAR and calls `finalizeWarStart()`
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:123:- Sends a gold/yellow server-wide message: *"War Restored: The war for [colony] has been resumed after server restart."*
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:145:Placed before TickScheduler shutdown because the war state must be captured while timers are still valid. Also wrapped in try/catch.
.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:151:**Location:** `config/warntax/active_wars.json`

.\wiki\War_Persistence.md:207:| Multiple wars active | All are independently saved and restored |

.\wiki\Espionage_System.md:15:- You are limited to `SpyMaxActivePerPlayer` (default: 3) active missions at once. You cannot send two spies to the same target colony simultaneously.
.\wiki\Espionage_System.md:19:> **Screenshot placeholder:** *The espionage tab in the colony management GUI showing an active spy mission â€” ACTIVE status with the three intel tier indicators on the right, and the target colony name and field time displayed*
.\wiki\Espionage_System.md:27:| Early | `IntelEarlyThresholdMinutes` (default: 2 min) | Colony name, citizen count, building count, whether the colony is at war |
.\wiki\Espionage_System.md:31:The longer your spy stays deployed, the more detailed the picture you get. Early intel is enough for a quick assessment before a raid. Late intel gives you a full strategic picture for a war.
.\wiki\Espionage_System.md:43:- The spy pathfinds toward the nearest exit from the colony
.\wiki\Espionage_System.md:50:You can recall an active spy at any time from the GUI. Recalling initiates a return journey (same travel time as deployment). Intel gathered up to the moment of recall is fully preserved once they return.
.\wiki\Espionage_System.md:73:The spy bribes a number of the target colonyâ€™s guards. On the targetâ€™s **next raid**, the bribed guards receive Weakness II and Slowness II debuffs for the entire raid duration, making them significantly less effective at defending. Bribe counts accumulate from multiple missions. The effect is consumed when the next raid begins.
.\wiki\Espionage_System.md:76:On successful completion, your colony receives a **tax income bonus** (default: +20%) for a configurable number of hours. Only one active steal buff can exist per colony at a time; a new steal mission overwrites the previous one.
.\wiki\Espionage_System.md:84:If JourneyMap is installed, active spy missions automatically create waypoints on your map â€” one marker at your colony (origin) and one at the target colony. Waypoint labels and colors update based on mission status (traveling, active, fleeing). Waypoints are removed when the mission ends.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:3:Wars leave a mark on your colony's economy long after the fighting stops. This page explains the three post-war economic systems: war exhaustion (reduced tax generation during and after war), war reparations (a harsher penalty for repeat losers), and war weariness protection (a comeback mechanic for severely weakened colonies).
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:15:While your colony is at war, tax generation is reduced by `WarTaxReductionPercent` (default: 30%). If your colony normally earns 1,000 coins per tax cycle, it earns 700 instead. This applies for the entire duration of the war.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:17:Additionally, immediately after a war ends in a loss or stalemate, the colony's tax generation is skipped entirely for `WarTaxFreezeCycles` (default: 3) tax cycles. At the default interval of 60 minutes per cycle, that is 3 skipped cycles â€” approximately 3 hours with no income.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:21:After the freeze cycles complete, recovery begins. The colony does not snap back to full income immediately. Instead, tax generation climbs linearly from the war-level reduced rate back to 100% over `PostWarRecoveryHours` (default: 48 hours).
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:23:For example, with a 30% war reduction and a 48-hour recovery period:
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:28:Recovery state persists through server restarts. The mod saves the war-end timestamp and continues the linear climb on next startup.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:36:Reparations are a separate, stacking penalty triggered only by repeated losses. A single war loss does not trigger reparations.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:40:If a colony loses `ReparationsTriggerLossesCount` (default: 3) wars within a rolling 7-day window, the reparations debuff activates immediately. The loss counter resets once reparations are applied, so reparations cannot stack on top of themselves from the same streak.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:50:If a colony is vassalized as the outcome of a war loss, the ongoing vassal tribute replaces the reparations debuff. The two penalties do not stack â€” a vassalized colony pays tribute instead of suffering the reparations tax cut.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:62:Every time a colony loses a war, the mod checks the colony's current tax balance. If that balance is at or below `WarWearinessThreshold` (default: 500 coins), the colony is granted temporary immunity from war declarations for `WarWearinessImmunityHours` (default: 24 hours).
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:65:- No other player can declare war on the protected colony
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:66:- The protected colony also cannot declare war on others
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:70:> Note: War immunity is not automatic after every loss. It only triggers when the colony's tax balance is at or below the threshold at the moment of defeat. A wealthy colony that loses a war receives no immunity.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:76:All three systems can be active on the same colony simultaneously. The mod applies them in this order:
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:78:1. **Active war:** tax multiplier reduced by `WarTaxReductionPercent`
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:82:A combined cap of `MaxCombinedWarPenaltyPercent` (default: 50%) prevents the stacked penalties from exceeding half of normal income. On top of that, a hard floor of 10% tax generation is enforced â€” no colony can be reduced to zero income by war penalties alone.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:84:The global `MinTaxGenerationPercent` (default: 30%) acts as a wider safety net across all penalty sources (raids, events, and war), ensuring colonies always earn at least 30% of their base income regardless of how many systems are penalizing them at once.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:88:A colony under reparations that also loses another war immediately:
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:90:- Active war reduction (30%): 700 coins
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:94:- Result: 560 coins per cycle until the war ends, then linear recovery while reparations continue
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:104:| `EnableWarExhaustion` | true | Master toggle for war exhaustion and recovery |
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:105:| `WarTaxReductionPercent` | 0.30 | Tax reduction during active war (0.0â€“1.0) |
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:107:| `PostWarRecoveryHours` | 48 | Hours to fully recover from war-level tax reduction |
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:116:| `WarWearinessImmunityHours` | 24 | Hours of war immunity granted to eligible colonies |
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:122:**Minimize exhaustion duration:** End wars quickly. The exhaustion recovery timer starts the moment the war ends. A war that drags on for 2 hours delays your recovery by 2 hours compared to one that ends in 20 minutes.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:124:**Avoid triggering reparations:** Three losses in seven days is the threshold. If you lost two wars recently, avoid aggressive play until the 7-day window resets. The loss history is per-colony, so losses are tracked individually.
.\wiki\War_Exhaustion.md:130:**Negotiate peace:** If you are losing a war and already carry one or two recent losses, settling via a peace treaty before the third loss prevents reparations from triggering entirely. See [War System](War_System) for peace proposal commands.
.\wiki\Easy_Factions_Integration.md:12:- Optionally, the faction owner and faction officers can be promoted to the **Officer** rank on every faction member's colony. This is **off by default** because Officer rank grants tax-claim rights (see warning below).
.\wiki\Easy_Factions_Integration.md:21:- **Active wars, raids, or sieges.** While a war, raid, or siege is underway, the integration skips that colony entirely. It also skips any individual player who is currently a participant in any active war, even on other colonies. This guarantees the integration never races the cleanup the war/raid/siege systems perform when those events end.
.\wiki\Easy_Factions_Integration.md:28:All keys live in the `Easy Factions Integration` section of `config/warntax/minecolonytax.toml`:
.\wiki\Easy_Factions_Integration.md:34:| `EasyFactionsPromoteOfficers`    | `false`  | If `true`, the faction owner and faction officers get the **Officer** rank (see warning above).      |
.\wiki\Easy_Factions_Integration.md:39:- The integration uses pure reflection against Easy Factions, so updates to Easy Factions do not require a rebuild of War 'N Taxes. If a future Easy Factions update renames the relevant API methods, the integration will silently disable itself and log a warning rather than crash.

.\wiki\Tax_Policies.md:27:| `/wnt taxpolicy` | Shows your colony's current policy and its active modifiers |
.\wiki\Tax_Policies.md:49:Use this when your colony is recovering from war or a raid, when happiness has dropped low, or when you want to build goodwill before a difficult period. The happiness benefit can reduce the chance of negative random events that require low happiness as a trigger condition.
.\wiki\Tax_Policies.md:58:Use this when you need to fill your treasury quickly and can absorb the happiness cost. Be aware that staying on High Tax for extended periods can trigger negative random events such as Corrupt Official and Guard Desertion, both of which require High or War Economy policy as a condition.
.\wiki\Tax_Policies.md:62:Maximum revenue at a significant happiness cost. Intended for active wartime use.
.\wiki\Tax_Policies.md:67:Use this during active wars when you need sustained treasury income to cover war expenses. This policy also enables the War Profiteering random event, which can add a further temporary revenue bonus. The happiness penalty is severe â€” monitor your colony happiness if you plan to hold this policy for more than a few tax cycles. Events like Labor Strike and Guard Desertion both list War Economy policy as a trigger condition.
.\wiki\Tax_Policies.md:75:The happiness modifier is additive to your colony's average happiness growth. The colony happiness scale runs from 0 to 10. A modifier of +0.20 nudges that average upward; -0.25 nudges it downward. This interacts with the existing happiness system â€” it does not override it or set a fixed value.
.\wiki\Tax_Policies.md:83:- **War Profiteering** â€” only triggers when War Economy policy is active; adds a temporary +35% tax bonus
.\wiki\Tax_Policies.md:94:Server administrators can adjust all policy modifiers in the config file (`config/warntax/minecolonytax.toml`) under the `Tax Policies` section. The system can also be disabled entirely with the `EnableTaxPolicies` key, in which case all colonies behave as if they are on Normal policy.

.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:3:Below is a list of all server configurations for War 'N Taxes. All settings live in `config/warntax/minecolonytax.toml` on the server.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:10:- **Description**: Enable SDMShop economy integration. When true, tax claims and war payouts use SDMShop balances. When false, physical currency items are used instead.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:30:- **Description**: Enable console logging of tax generation details (building upgrades, cap warnings, etc.). Set to false to reduce console spam. Controlled by the LogLevel setting above.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:38:- **Description**: Amount added to colony debt per guard killed when raiding colonies already in debt. Only applies when DebtLimit > 0.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:42:- **Description**: Enable colony ownership transfer when a war is won.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:46:- **Description**: If false, war will not toggle any colony interaction permissions.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:50:- **Description**: If true, war declarations must be manually accepted by the defender. If false, wars start immediately with no option to refuse.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:54:- **Description**: Grace period between declaring wars (minutes). After declaring a war, the attacker cannot declare another for this duration.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:58:- **Description**: Grace period between raids (minutes). After a raid, this player cannot raid again for this duration.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:62:- **Description**: Maximum raid duration in minutes. The raid ends automatically when this time expires.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:66:- **Description**: Penalty percentage applied to a raider's balance when killed by a defender during a raid (0.0-1.0).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:69:### RaidDefenseRewardPercentage
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:70:- **Description**: Percentage of the killed raider's balance transferred to the defending colony owner or officers to claim (0.0-1.0).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:74:- **Description**: Percentage of losing players' balance awarded to each winning player. Set to 0.0 to only enable colony transfer (if enabled).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:78:- **Description**: Percentage each losing player loses from their balance when defeated in war. Should match WarVictoryPercentage to prevent money creation.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:82:- **Description**: Percentage all war participants lose from their balance when a war ends in a draw.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:86:- **Description**: (Deprecated â€” use WarTaxFreezeCycles instead.) Duration in hours to freeze colony tax generation after a war loss or stalemate. Set to 0 to disable. Ignored if WarTaxFreezeCycles is greater than 0.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:90:- **Description**: Number of tax cycles to skip after a war loss or stalemate. Cycle-based freezing ensures consistent behavior regardless of TaxIntervalMinutes. At default 60-minute intervals, 3 cycles = 3 hours. Takes precedence over WarTaxFreezeHours.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:94:- **Description**: Maximum combined penalty from war exhaustion and active-war tax reduction (0.0-1.0). Prevents excessive stacking. Example: 0.5 = 50% maximum total penalty.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:98:- **Description**: Minimum tax generation floor as a fraction of base generation (0.0-1.0). After all penalties stack (raid, war exhaustion, reparations, events), tax income will never drop below this fraction. Prevents permanent economic collapse.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:102:- **Description**: Allow players to raid colonies when the colony owner is offline.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:114:- **Description**: When enabled, the attacker's colony becomes a WAGER in every war. If the defender wins, the attacker's colony enters an occupied state controlled by the defender. This creates high-risk warfare where aggressors cannot safely bully weaker players.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:118:- **Description**: When enabled and EnableColonyTransfer is disabled, winning a war will vassalize the losing colony instead of transferring ownership. The losing colony pays a percentage of their tax income to the winner for a set duration.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:126:- **Description**: Duration in hours that a war vassalization lasts. After this time the vassalization ends automatically. Set to 0 for permanent vassalization until manually revoked.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:130:- **Description**: Minimum number of guards required to initiate a raid. Only used when EnableRaidBuildingRequirements is disabled. If building requirements are enabled, they take priority.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:134:- **Description**: When enabled, colonies must meet minimum defense requirements to be eligible as raid targets. Protects smaller or newer colonies from being overwhelmed.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:138:- **Description**: Minimum number of guards a colony must have before it can be raided. Set to 0 to disable.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:142:- **Description**: Minimum number of guard towers a colony must have before it can be raided. Set to 0 to disable.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:146:- **Description**: Interval in seconds between automatic tax transfers during a raid.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:150:- **Description**: Enable entity-triggered raids. When disabled, hostile entity groups near a colony will not trigger a raid even if they meet the criteria. Disabled by default.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:154:- **Description**: List of entity types that can trigger raids. Use Minecraft entity resource IDs (e.g., 'minecraft:pillager'). Default: only Pillagers.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:158:- **Description**: Number of whitelisted entities near a colony required to trigger an entity raid.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:162:- **Description**: Radius in blocks to scan around colonies for entity raid detection.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:166:- **Description**: If true, entity raids only send alert messages to the colony without triggering actual raid mechanics.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:170:- **Description**: Seconds entities have to return to colony boundaries after leaving during an active entity raid.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:178:- **Description**: Cooldown in minutes between entity raids for the same colony.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:182:- **Description**: Enable detailed debug logging for the entity raid system.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:186:- **Description**: Verbosity of entity raid debug logging. 1 = basic, 2 = detailed, 3 = verbose.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:190:- **Description**: Testing only. Bypass alliance checks to allow your own recruits to trigger raids. Keep false in production.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:194:- **Description**: When enabled, killing a player in war transfers a percentage of their balance to the killer. Compatible with SDMShop and SDMEconomy. Disabled by default.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:197:### PvPKillRewardPercentage
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:210:- **Description**: When enabled, guards receive a resistance effect during active raids to help defend the colony.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:214:- **Description**: Level of resistance applied to guards during raids (0-255). Higher = more protection. Set to 0 to disable the effect while keeping the feature enabled.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:238:- **Description**: Enable extortion. When declaring war, the attacker can demand a percentage of the defender's balance as payment to call off the war.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:246:- **Description**: Minutes the defender has to respond to an extortion demand before the war starts automatically.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:254:- **Description**: When enabled, a configurable portion of eligible citizens convert into temporary militia guards during raids.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:258:- **Description**: Fraction of eligible citizens converted into militia during raids (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.3 = 30%.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:262:- **Description**: Minimum citizen job level required to be eligible for militia conversion.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:266:- **Description**: If true, militia and guards actively chase raiders instead of defending only their assigned posts.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:274:- **Description**: Percentage of colony tax stolen per guard or militia killed during a raid (0.0-1.0).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:278:- **Description**: Maximum total percentage of colony tax that can be stolen in a single raid (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.25 = 25% max when all defenders are killed.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:282:- **Description**: If true, the resistance effect during raids and wars is also applied to all citizens, not only guards.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:294:- **Description**: If true, owners and officers receive warnings when they log in during the pre-abandonment window.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:298:- **Description**: Days before the abandonment deadline during which warning notifications are sent on login.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:310:- **Description**: When enabled, players can claim abandoned colonies using /wnt claimcolony, triggering a raid where all citizens become hostile.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:318:- **Description**: Duration of the claiming raid in minutes. The claimer must survive this long and eliminate all defenders to succeed.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:334:- **Description**: When enabled, building requirements take priority over MinGuardsToRaid for determining raid eligibility.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:338:- **Description**: Building requirements to initiate a raid. Format: 'building:level:amount'. Example: 'townhall:1:1,guardtower:1:3'. Leave empty to disable.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:342:- **Description**: When enabled, building requirements take priority over MinGuardsToWageWar for determining war eligibility.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:346:- **Description**: Building requirements to declare war. Format: 'building:level:amount'. Example: 'townhall:2:1,guardtower:1:3,buildershut:1:1,house:1:1'. Leave empty to disable.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:354:- **Description**: Enable the MySQL/MariaDB statistics database. When enabled, war results, raid history, kills, and colony state are written to a shared database that your website container can also query. Both the game server and the website connect to the same database via TCP â€” no file sharing required. Get credentials from the Pterodactyl panel under server > Databases. Default: false
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:366:- **Description**: Name of the database to write to. Copy from the Pterodactyl Databases tab. The mod creates all required tables automatically on first startup. Default: warntax
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:367:- **Default Value**: warntax
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:370:- **Description**: Database username. Copy from the Pterodactyl Databases tab. Default: warntax
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:371:- **Default Value**: warntax
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:410:- **Description**: Revenue modifier for the WAR ECONOMY tax policy. High boost during wartime. Example: 0.50 = 50% more revenue.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:430:- **Description**: Enable server-wide leaderboards for tax earnings, wars won, etc.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:490:- **Description**: Maximum number of active trade routes a colony can have.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:506:- **Description**: Maximum number of concurrent active spy missions per player.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:522:- **Description**: Treasury cost to deploy a BRIBE GUARDS spy (disables a number of guards before the target's next raid defense).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:534:- **Description**: Minutes a SABOTAGE spy must remain active before the sabotage takes effect. Spies detected before this threshold apply no effect on escape.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:562:- **Description**: Minutes a spy must be active before Tier 1 intel is gathered (colony name, citizen count, building count, war status).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:566:- **Description**: Minutes a spy must be active before Tier 2 intel is gathered (guard count, happiness, tax balance).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:570:- **Description**: Minutes a spy must be active before Tier 3 intel is gathered (owner balance, officer list, full member list).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:606:- **Description**: Enable the treasury system. Colonies must have funds in the treasury to declare war. The treasury drains during active wars.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:610:- **Description**: Minimum treasury balance required as a percentage of the target colony's tax balance (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.25 = need 25% of target's balance to declare war.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:618:- **Description**: Flat amount drained from treasury per minute during active war. Only used when TreasuryDrainUsePercent is false. At default (10/min on a 25k treasury), a war lasts approximately 4 hours.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:626:- **Description**: Percentage of treasury max capacity drained per minute during active war (0.0-1.0). Only used when TreasuryDrainUsePercent is true. Example: 0.004 = 0.4% of max capacity per minute.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:634:- **Description**: If true, war automatically ends in surrender when the treasury is depleted.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:642:- **Description**: Fraction by which the defending colony's treasury drain is reduced during war (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.5 = defender drains at half the normal rate (home field advantage).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:646:- **Description**: If true, raids require treasury funds. Cost is a one-time payment based on the target's tax generation.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:650:- **Description**: Raid cost as a percentage of the target colony's tax per interval (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.10 = raiding costs 10% of what target earns per tax cycle.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:654:- **Description**: Percentage reduction in tax generation for a raided colony (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.25 = 25% less tax after being raided.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:658:- **Description**: Duration in hours that the post-raid tax penalty lasts.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:662:- **Description**: Cost to repair colony and remove raid penalty early, as a percentage of colony's total tax earnings (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.10 = repairing costs 10% of colony's tax balance.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:666:- **Description**: Enable war exhaustion. Colonies generate less tax during active wars and need recovery time afterward.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:670:- **Description**: Percentage reduction in tax generation during an active war (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.30 = 30% less tax.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:674:- **Description**: Hours after a war ends for colony tax generation to fully recover to normal.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:678:- **Description**: Enable the war reparations debuff for colonies that lose wars frequently within a short window.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:686:- **Description**: Duration in hours that the war reparations debuff lasts.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:690:- **Description**: Number of wars lost within 7 days to trigger the reparations debuff.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:694:- **Description**: Enable war weariness protection. Colonies with very low tax balance that lost a war receive temporary war immunity to allow economic recovery (comeback mechanic).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:698:- **Description**: Tax balance at or below which a colony qualifies for war weariness immunity after losing a war.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:702:- **Description**: Hours of war declaration immunity granted to a colony below the weariness threshold after losing a war.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:706:- **Description**: If true, when a colony is vassalized after a war loss, the ongoing tribute replaces the one-time reparations payment, preventing double-punishment.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:710:- **Description**: Enable ransom system. When the colony owner dies during a raid, the attacker can demand a ransom payment to end the raid early.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:734:- **Description**: Hours of immunity from raids granted to a player after they pay a ransom.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:762:- **Description**: Guard damage bonus while training is active (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.10 = +10% damage.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:786:- **Description**: Bonus to spy detection chance while research is active (0.0-1.0). Example: 0.50 = 50% higher detection chance.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:797:Colonies can spend treasury funds to permanently improve their capabilities. Upgrades are purchased via `/wnt invest buy <type>` and persist across server restarts in `config/warntax/colony_upgrades.json`.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:880:- **Description**: Fraction of incoming raid damage reduced per Fortification upgrade level (0.05 = 5%). Capped at 75% total.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:896:- **Description**: Enable the besiege system. Allows players to raid active non-primary colonies and establish tax vassalage on victory.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:900:- **Description**: Duration of a besiege raid in minutes. Defenders must survive this long to repel the attack.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:904:- **Description**: Hours a player must wait after a besiege attempt (win or loss) before besieging again.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:908:- **Description**: Fraction of eligible citizens converted to militia defenders during a besiege (0.0-1.0).
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:912:- **Description**: Percentage of tax income siphoned from the besieged colony to the victor each tax cycle.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:916:- **Description**: How long (hours) the besiege vassalage lasts. Set to 0 for permanent until the colony is reclaimed.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:920:- **Description**: Minimum citizen count required in the target colony before it can be besieged.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:924:- **Description**: Allow other players to assist the besieger by attacking defenders. They are tracked as allies and also hunted.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:932:- **Description**: Maximum number of mercenaries that can be spawned during a single besiege raid.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:936:- **Description**: Maximum distance in blocks the besieging player may stray from the colony center. Exceeding this cancels the raid.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:956:- **Description**: Maximum number of events that can be active simultaneously per colony.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:993:- **Description**: Enable the Merchant Caravan event (+15% tax, +0.3 happiness for 2 cycles). Requires 3 or more restaurants or taverns and no active war.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:997:- **Description**: War duration in minutes. The war ends automatically if neither side is eliminated before this time.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1001:- **Description**: Minimum guards required to declare war. Only used when EnableWarBuildingRequirements is disabled.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1005:- **Description**: When enabled, war participants are moved to the 'war' LuckPerms permission group during active wars. Requires LuckPerms installed and a 'war' group configured.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1009:- **Description**: Duration of the join phase in minutes. During this window, allies can join the war before active combat begins.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1013:- **Description**: When enabled, players keep their inventory when they die on their last life during a war, preventing permanent gear loss in colony transfer scenarios.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1017:- **Description**: Number of lives each player has during a war. Losing all lives switches the player to spectator mode for the remainder of the war.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1021:- **Description**: Colony permission actions that are granted to enemy players during an active war. See the MineColonies Action API for valid values.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1025:- **Description**: Colony permission actions that are granted to raiders during an active raid.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1029:- **Description**: Colony permission actions granted to the claiming player during an abandoned colony claiming raid.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1033:- **Description**: Enable the block interaction filter system during raids and wars. Blacklisted blocks cannot be interacted with at all; whitelisted blocks can be opened even when other permissions would deny it.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1037:- **Description**: List of block IDs that cannot be interacted with during raids and wars (highest priority). Format: 'modid:blockname' for a specific block, or '#modid' to block an entire mod. Blacklist overrides whitelist.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1041:- **Description**: List of block IDs that can be interacted with during raids and wars even when other permissions would deny it. Format: 'modid:blockname' or '#modid' for an entire mod. Blacklist always takes priority over whitelist.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1045:- **Description**: Apply block interaction filter rules during active wars.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1049:- **Description**: Apply block interaction filter rules during active raids.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1138:- **Description**: Controls how much the mod prints to the server console. `0` = Errors and warnings only. `1` = Normal informational messages. `2` = Full debug output including detailed calculations.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1146:- **Description**: When true, winning a war puts the defeated colony into an Occupation phase rather than transferring it immediately. The occupier collects a share of taxes while the original owner has a window to reclaim their colony.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1166:- **Description**: When true, the attacker's colony is wagered in every war declaration. If the defender wins, the attacker's colony enters Occupation instead of the defender's.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1174:- **Description**: Number of tax cycles that tax generation is frozen or penalised after a war loss. Replaces the older hours-based freeze setting.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1178:- **Description**: Maximum combined percentage penalty that can be applied to a colony's tax generation from stacked war debuffs (exhaustion, reparations, etc.). Prevents death spirals.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1196:See [WarDefenderDrainReduction](#wardefenderdrainreduction) in the Treasury section above.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1203:- **Description**: When true, players who have been targeted for war too many times recently gain temporary immunity from further war declarations.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1207:- **Description**: Number of war-related actions (hits against a colony) that must accumulate before war weariness immunity is granted.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1211:- **Description**: How many hours of war declaration immunity a colony receives once the weariness threshold is reached. Range: 1â€“168.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1235:- **Description**: Maximum number of active spy missions a single player can have running at once.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1273:- **Description**: Master toggle for the besiege system. When disabled, `/wnt besiege` is rejected.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1277:- **Description**: How long (minutes) the besieger has to kill all defenders. If the timer runs out, defenders win.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1281:- **Description**: How long (hours) a player must wait after any besiege attempt before they can besiege again.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1289:- **Description**: Percentage of the besieged colony's tax income siphoned to the victor each tax cycle.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1293:- **Description**: How many hours the besiege vassalage lasts before it expires automatically. Set to 0 for permanent until reclaimed.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1297:- **Description**: Minimum number of citizens a target colony must have before it can be besieged.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1309:- **Description**: Maximum total mercenaries that can be spawned in a single besiege raid.
.\wiki\Configuration_Guide.md:1313:- **Description**: Maximum distance (blocks) from the colony centre the besieger may stray. Exceeding this cancels the raid.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:14:- **Tax Floor:** No matter how many penalties are stacked against your colony (war exhaustion, raid penalties, labor strikes, etc.), tax generation will never fall below **30%** of its base value. This prevents permanent economic collapse from compounding debts.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:17:If enabled (`EnableHappinessTaxModifier`), your Colony's **real Minecolonies Citizen Happiness** acts as the ultimate multiplier on your gross tax revenue. The mod reads the actual per-citizen happiness scores from Minecolonies (housing, food, security, health, employment, etc.), averages them across all adult citizens, and applies any active Tax Policy or Random Event modifiers on top.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:21:- **How it works:** A colony happiness of **5.0** (neutral) produces a **1.0x** tax multiplier â€” no bonus, no penalty. Below 5 penalizes revenue; above 5 rewards it.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:23:- **Happy Citizens:** Maintaining perfect happiness rewards you. By default (`HappinessTaxMultiplierMax`), maximum happiness boosts your gross revenue to **150% efficiency** (1.5x multiplier) at happiness 10.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:24:- **What affects happiness:** Everything in Minecolonies matters â€” food diversity, housing, employment, guard-to-citizen ratio, health, sleep, education, and more. On top of that, your active Tax Policy and any Random Events apply additive modifiers to the colony average.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:29:- **Going into Debt:** If your colony is heavily raided, sabotaged, or loses wars, you can sink into negative balances.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:34:Colony leaders can actively control output versus stability by enforcing specific **Tax Policies**. Policy happiness modifiers are **additive** to the colony's average happiness on a 0â€“10 scale â€” the effect is fixed and predictable.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:38:- **War Economy:** The ultimate desperate lever. **+50% revenue**, used to fund active wars, but subtracts **0.25 happiness** from the colony average.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:43:- **Trade Routes:** Factions can establish active trade routes between allied colonies.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:45:  - Maximum route distance is **100 chunks**; a maximum of **2 routes** can be active at once per colony.
.\wiki\Taxation_System.md:52:* `/wnt checktax` : View your current generation speed, active multipliers, and total treasury.
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:15:| `/wnt wagewar <colony> [extortion%]` | Declares war on a specified colony. Requires certain building levels or guards. Optionally demand extortion. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:16:| `/wnt raid <colony>` | Starts a quick raid on a target colony. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:17:| `/wnt joinwar` | Join an active war. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:18:| `/wnt leavewar` | Leave your current war engagement. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:19:| `/wnt payextortion <colonyId> <extortion%>` | Pay requested extortion to avoid an incoming war. The percent must match the attacker's demand. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:20:| `/wnt war accept <colonyId>` | Accept a pending war declaration. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:21:| `/wnt war decline <colonyId>` | Decline a pending war declaration. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:24:| `/wnt peace surrender` | Unconditionally surrender the war, accepting full defeat penalties immediately. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:27:| `/wnt warinfo` | Show detailed information about your current active war. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:33:| `/wnt warhistory [colony]` | View your colony's war history. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:34:| `/wnt raidhistory [colony]` | View your colony's raid history. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:35:| `/wnt warstats` | View your personal PvP and war statistics. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:43:| `/wnt besiege <colony>` | Besiege a target non-primary colony. On victory, siphons a portion of their taxes. Former owner can use this same command to reclaim their besieged colony. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:45:| `/wnt claimcolony [colony]` | Claim an abandoned colony by starting a claiming raid against it. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:50:| `/wnt spy recall <missionId>` | Recall an active or traveling spy. Traveling spies cancel immediately; active spies begin a return journey. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:51:| `/wnt spy status` | List all your active and recently completed spy missions with status and gathered intel summary. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:53:| `/wnt treasury status [colonyId]` | View treasury balance, drain rate, war sustainability, and available deposit sources. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:61:| `/wnt events <colonyId>` | View all active random events for a colony, including their remaining duration and effects. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:72:| `/wnt warstop <colony>` | Force-stop a specific war involving the given colony. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:73:| `/wnt warstopall` | Force-stop all currently active wars on the server. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:74:| `/wnt raidstop` | Force-stop any active raids currently executing. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:79:| `/wnt claimraidstatus <colony>` | Check the status of a claiming raid on a colony. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:83:| `/wnt debugbossbar <colony>` | Debug the boss bar state for the war involving a colony. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:84:| `/wnt forcecleanupcolony <colony>` | Force a full cleanup of a colony's war/raid state. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:85:| `/wnt emergencyfix` | Emergency fix for broken war state on the server. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:88:| `/wnt debug war` | Show deeply technical debug information for all active wars. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:92:| `/wnt debug besiege` | Show active besiege and occupation status across all colonies. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:93:| `/wnt debug entityraid status` | Show the status of active entity (PvE) raids. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:94:| `/wnt debug entityraid config` | Show the current configuration limits and rules for entity raids. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:95:| `/wnt debug entityraid end <colonyId>` | End an active entity raid for a colony. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:96:| `/wnt debug entityraid test <colony>` | Force-trigger an entity raid to test mechanics. |
.\wiki\Commands_&_Permissions.md:97:| `/wnt debug entityraid reload` | Reload the entity raid configuration dynamically. |

.\wiki\Random_Events.md:11:Rulers are occasionally blessed by unforeseen fortune. These events reward investment in infrastructure, high happiness, and stable policy.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:15:    *   *Conditions:* 3 or more restaurants or taverns. Cannot trigger during war.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:31:    *   *Conditions:* Happiness above 7.0. Cannot trigger during war.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:35:    *   *Conditions:* Colony has more than 500 stored taxes. Cannot trigger during war.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:39:    *   *Conditions:* Happiness above 6.0 and more than 30 citizens. Cannot trigger during war.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:83:One event only triggers during active wars.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:87:    *   *Conditions:* Colony is on WAR_ECONOMY policy and is actively at war.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:124:The colony's active tax policy shifts the odds of positive and negative events:
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:135:*   **During an active raid:** No events fire at all.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:136:*   **During an active war:** All events are 50% less likely, except War Profiteering which fires at normal rate.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:137:*   **Post-war recovery:** While war exhaustion is active, negative events are 50% less likely.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:143:The base probability for each event is scaled by `BaseChanceMultiplier` (configurable, range 0.5-2.0). A global cooldown prevents events from clustering, and each event type has its own cooldown to prevent repeats. `MaxSimultaneousEvents` caps how many events can be active at once per colony. `ProtectNewColoniesHours` provides a grace period before events can target a newly founded colony.
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:157:| `/wnt events <colonyId>` | Lists all active events, remaining cycles, and effects. Requires officer rank or above. |
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:159:### Admin Commands (OP required)
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:164:| `/wnt events reset <colonyId>` | Resets all event state for a colony: clears new-colony protection, all cooldowns, and active events. Use this to start a fresh testing session without waiting for the 24-hour protection window. |
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:177:2. `/wnt triggerevent 1 BANDIT_HARASSMENT` â€” immediately trigger a bandit raid
.\wiki\Random_Events.md:178:3. `/wnt events 1` â€” verify the event is active and check remaining cycles
.\wiki\Colony_Abandonment.md:3:In long-running servers, inactive players naturally leave behind ghost-town colonies. The **Colony Abandonment** system allows active players to strategically purge and reclaim these dead plots, redistributing wealth and land back into the active economy.
.\wiki\Colony_Abandonment.md:7:- **Inactivity Threshold:** If an Owner or Officer has not physically visited their colony chunks for a configurable number of days (default: **14 days** via `ColonyAutoAbandonDays`), the server initiates the abandonment process. A separate setting, `ColonyInactivityHoursThreshold` (default: 168 hours = 1 week), controls when tax generation pauses for inactive colonies â€” this is independent of the full abandonment trigger.
.\wiki\Colony_Abandonment.md:8:- **Warnings:** If `NotifyOwnersBeforeAbandon` is true, logging into the server during the final warning period (default: **3 Days** before via `AbandonWarningDays`) will blast urgent notifications to the leaders.
.\wiki\Colony_Abandonment.md:24:3. The defending militia will swarm and relentlessly hunt the claiming player for a specified duration (`ClaimingRaidDurationMinutes`).
.\wiki\Colony_Abandonment.md:28:If the claiming player survives the duration of the raid without dying and successfully executes all hostiles, the massive blood-toll is considered paid! The `ColonyOwnershipHandler` instantly transfers full ownership of the town, all its structures, and any remaining treasury funds over to the victor.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:5:## 1. Initiating a Raid (`/wnt raid <colony>`)
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:6:Just like Wars, Raiding relies on server configuration to strike a balance between Risk and Reward. 
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:7:- **Building Dependencies:** Attackers must meet a defined quota of military infrastructure (like level 2 Guard Towers) to trigger the `/wnt raid` command (`RaidBuildingRequirements`).
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:8:- **Defending Limitations:** `EnableRaidGuardProtection` prevents veteran cities from easily wiping out infant towns. Target colonies usually require a minimum count of specific buildings (e.g. **1 Guard Tower** `MinGuardTowersToBeRaided`) or active guards (e.g. **2 Guards** `MinGuardsToBeRaided`) before they are eligible to be raided.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:11:During an active raid, the primary objective is not to capture a flag or kill the owner. Your goal is to bleed their Treasury dry by slaying defenders.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:13:- **Raid Caps:** The system prevents complete wipeouts. A raid will forcefully cap out after stealing a maximum threshold, typically **50%** (`MaxRaidTaxPercentage`) of the colonyâ€™s total tax. Once you hit that cap, further guard kills yield no money.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:16:Unlike standard Minecolonies where citizens flee into buildings during night-time raids, War 'N Taxes empowers them!
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:17:- When a raid initiates, a flat **30%** (`MilitiaConversionPercentage`) of the targeted colony's standard civilian population immediately converts into heavily-armed temporary guards.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:20:- Once the raid reaches its `MaxRaidDurationMinutes`, any surviving Militia immediately revert back to their peaceful civilian duties.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:24:- **Attacker Penalties:** If the defending Owner, Officer, Guard, or Militia member successfully kills an attacker during the raid window, the attacker suffers a massive financial penalty, usually dropping **25%** (`RaidPenaltyPercentage`) of their personal balance.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:25:- **Defender Reward:** The server then takes that stripped wealth and actively rewards the successful defenders (`RaidDefenseRewardPercentage`), directly injecting the attacker's drained cash into the colony.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:29:If an attacker successfully raids a colony and escapes with the loot, the colony's economy crumbles.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:30:- **Tax Reduction:** The raided colony natively takes a massive hit to all tax regeneration cycles for the next several hours due to panic and stolen logistics (typically a **25%** reduction via `RaidPenaltyTaxReductionPercent`).
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:31:- **Owner Ransoms (`EnableRansomSystem`):** A brutal mechanic. If the defending Owner or Officer is slain by the attacker during the raid, the attacker can demand a **Ransom**. They freeze the raid timer and demand a massive percentage of the defenderâ€™s balance (default **15%** `RansomDefaultPercent`). The defender has mere seconds (`RansomTimeoutSeconds`) to respond by typing a command, or hostilities immediately resume.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:35:- If enabled (`EnableEntityRaids`), natural hostile spawns like Pillager patrols wandering within **50 blocks** of your borders (`EntityRaidDetectionRadius`) can dynamically trigger massive NPC raid sequences directly on your colony.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:36:- These mobs will attempt to slaughter your guards just like a player would, meaning they can actively ruin your tax generation if left unchecked.
.\wiki\Raid_System.md:37:- *Admins use `/wnt entityraid` commands to toggle whitelists, check cooldowns, or forcefully summon PvE raids for testing.*

.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:3:The Besiege system lets a player raid another player's non-primary colony and, on victory, extract tribute from it â€” without triggering a full server-wide war.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:9:Use **besiege** when you want to contest a player's secondary colony for tax income. Besieging is a single-player action (though allies can help) with lower political costs than war.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:11:**First (primary) colonies cannot be besieged.** To contest a player's primary colony you must declare full war.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:13:**Abandoned colonies cannot be besieged** â€” use the colony claiming raid for those.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:20:/wnt besiege <colony>
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:23:Requirements before the raid begins:
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:28:- The target must not already have an active besiege raid.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:38:1. **Guards** in the target colony turn hostile and hunt the besieger.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:43:The besieger has a limited window (default 20 minutes) to kill every defender. Leaving the colony area (beyond 100 blocks of centre) cancels the raid.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:49:> **Screenshot placeholder:** *The besiege in progress: boss bar at the top of the screen showing remaining defender count and timer, hostile guards charging the besieger*
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:56:| Timer runs out | Defenders win: besieger on cooldown |
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:57:| Besieger leaves the area | Raid cancelled: besieger on cooldown |
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:63:On a successful besiege:
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:65:- The target colony is **force-vassalized** â€” it pays a percentage of its tax income (default 30%) to the besieger each tax cycle.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:71:When a besiege starts:
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:73:- The **colony owner and all officers** receive a direct chat alert regardless of where they are on the server: "WARNING: [player] is besieging your colony [name]!"
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:74:- Players who happen to be physically **near the colony** see a separate area broadcast: "Nearby colony [name] is under siege by [player]!" â€” this is a local alert for bystanders, not a personal colony warning.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:75:- If the owner or an officer is **offline** when the besiege starts or completes, they receive a chat message and on-screen title alert the next time they log in.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:79:While the besiege is active, the **Events** tab in the colony management GUI shows a live entry at the top: **Under Siege by [player]** (red bar). Tax claiming is disabled for the colony during this time. The entry disappears automatically when the besiege ends.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:85:If your colony has been besieged, you can take it back:
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:88:/wnt besiege <your besieged colony>
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:91:The same raid plays out â€” you must kill all defenders within the time limit. If you win, the vassalage ends, the lockout is lifted, and your colony is fully restored.
.\wiki\Besiege_System.md:97:After any besiege attempt (win or loss), you must wait before attempting another (default 24 hours). This applies to both the initial besiege and reclaim attempts.

.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:5:The Occupation System is the default outcome when a war is won. Rather than instantly transferring the defeated colony to the victor, the colony enters an intermediate **Occupied** state. The winner gains economic benefits while the original owner retains full control and has time to fight back.
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:14:Occupation starts automatically when a war ends in victory for one side. Both players are notified in chat. Note that when the [Colony Wager](War_System#colony-wager-system) is active, the **attacker's** colony can also be occupied if the defender wins.
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:24:- Building requirements and treasury costs are waived for reclamation wars â€” the system recognises that a player fighting to reclaim their home may not have the resources for a standard war declaration
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:25:- If the reclamation war is won, the occupation ends immediately and the colony is fully restored to the original owner
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:26:- If the reclamation war is lost, ownership transfers to the occupier immediately (the reclamation window is forfeit)
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:29:If no reclamation war is attempted before the occupation window expires, **full ownership transfers automatically** to the occupier. No further action is required by either party.
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:32:Occupation state is saved to `config/warntax/occupations.json` and survives server restarts.
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:48:The **Events** tab for the occupied colony shows a non-dismissible entry at the top: **Occupied by [player]** in orange. This entry remains until the occupation ends, either through a successful reclamation war or automatic transfer when the window expires.
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:54:When `EnableColonyWager` is enabled (default: true), the attacker's colony is also wagered in every war. If the **defender wins**, the attacker's colony enters Occupation rather than the defender's. This means declaring war always carries real risk â€” the aggressor can end up occupied if they lose.
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:64:| `EnableOccupationSystem` | true | Enables the occupation phase after a war victory. If disabled, colony transfer happens immediately when `EnableColonyTransfer` is true. |
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:65:| `OccupationDurationDays` | 7 | Number of real-time days the original owner has to attempt a reclamation war before ownership transfers automatically. Range: 1â€“90. |
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:75:| Reclamation war won | Occupation ends; original owner fully restored |
.\wiki\Occupation_System.md:76:| Reclamation war lost | Ownership transfers immediately to occupier |
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:5:Investments are a strategic money sink â€” converting the Treasury reserves you accumulate between wars into lasting military, economic, or espionage advantages.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:45:All upgrade levels are saved to `config/warntax/colony_upgrades.json` and survive server restarts.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:53:Increases the proportion of citizens that convert into militia during raids.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:61:Increases the number of spy missions you can have active at the same time.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:63:- **Effect per level:** +1 additional active spy slot (`UpgradeSpyCapacityPerLevel`, default: 1)
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:77:Reduces the chance that your spies are detected while on active missions.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:85:Increases attacker effectiveness during raids, allowing more damage and pressure on the defending colony.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:87:- **Effect per level:** +10% raid force multiplier (`UpgradeRaidForceMultiplierPerLevel`, default: 0.10)
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:93:Increases the resistance buff applied to guards during raids and wars.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:117:Reduces incoming damage to the colony during sieges and raids. Capped at a maximum of 75% total reduction regardless of level.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:135:All upgrade configuration keys live under the `[ColonyUpgrades]` section in `config/warntax/minecolonytax.toml`.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:179:- **Invest in what you use.** SPY_CAPACITY and SPY_SPEED are only valuable if you actively run espionage missions. DEFENSE and FORTIFICATION pay off most during server conflicts.
.\wiki\Investments_System.md:181:- **COUNTER_INTEL is defensive espionage.** Colonies targeted by active spymasters should prioritize this â€” at level 5 there is a 50% chance any arriving spy is immediately neutralized.

.\minecolonies\README.md:10:MineColonies is an interactive building mod that allows you to create a thriving town within Minecraft. It lets your leadership skills soar by providing you with everything you need to build your kingdom. MineColonies gives you the flexibility to create a colony as unique as every player. With so many options, you'll create a different colony every time, adapt it to any biome, build inside a mountain, on top of one, under the ocean, or in the sky.

.\reviews\step-05-codex.md:14:Reviewing step 5 of 11. New LivingHurtEvent handler enforces 'solo besiege' on the attacker side only. Source = besieger's colony-mate (not the besieger themselves) AND target = defender-side â†’ cancel damage. Review for: (1) correctness of areColonyMates colony-walking logic â€” does it correctly identify mates without false positives on Neutral/Hostile rank players, (2) isDefenderSideTarget logic â€” does it cover all defender entity types correctly, (3) early returns ordering (hot path - this fires on EVERY damage event), (4) any way an attacker's ally could bypass this. Respond: STATUS, up to 5 bullets, up to 3 file:line fix suggestions. Max 300 words.
.\reviews\step-05-codex.md:17:## STEP 5 â€” Asymmetric solo besiege damage shield
.\reviews\step-05-codex.md:19:New file BesiegeDamageShieldHandler.java. Subscribes to LivingHurtEvent. If source is a player who is a colony-mate of any active besieger (but NOT the besieger themselves), and target is on the defender side (citizen or non-hostile player of the besieged colony), cancel the damage. One-way: defender allies are NOT blocked.

.\reviews\step-03-codex.md:14:Reviewing step 3 of an 11-step Java refactor (Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge mod, War 'N Taxes / MineColonies addon). Step 3 partially implements multi-besieger support by re-keying ACTIVE_RAIDS from colonyId to besiegerUUID and removing the primary-colony block + the double-besiege block. Phase 2 follow-ups are intentionally deferred (see bundle preamble). Review for: correctness of the re-keying (do all internal call sites consistently use the new key?), backward-compat correctness of getActiveRaids() view (does putIfAbsent semantics matter?), race conditions in the view construction, whether cleanupRaid still removes the correct entry, whether the iterator-based tick loop is still safe with the new key, and any caller of ACTIVE_RAIDS or BesiegeRaidData that the refactor may have missed. The Phase 2 deferrals (shared defender pool, last-kill-credit) are KNOWN gaps â€” please flag them but don't count them against the status. Respond: (1) STATUS APPROVE/REWORK/REJECT, (2) up to 5 bullet findings ranked by severity, (3) up to 3 file:line fix suggestions. Max 350 words.
.\reviews\step-03-codex.md:17:## STEP 3 REVIEW BUNDLE â€” Multi-besieger refactor (partial)
.\reviews\step-03-codex.md:19:Step 3 changes ACTIVE_RAIDS from Map<Integer, BesiegeRaidData> (colony-keyed, one raid per colony) to Map<UUID, BesiegeRaidData> (besieger-keyed). This unblocks multiple besiegers attacking the same colony concurrently AND allows besieging primary colonies (outcome routes via OccupationManager.TAX_ONLY from step 2). The legacy getActiveRaids() now returns a backward-compat colonyâ†’first-raid view. New getRaidsForColony() and getRaidForBesieger() helpers added.

.\reviews\step-03-codex.md:24:- Each besieger's raid still ends independently when their per-raid defender count hits zero.
